extraction.Name: Benjamin Janis
extraction.Refused/Protested: did not want the patent to his 320 acre allotment at the time he received it; but was advised by the Indian Agency that, if he did not take charge of it, it would be assessed for taxes, for which it would finally be sold, so he accepted it
extraction.Sold/Mortgaged: in 1922, he deeded his allotment to his son, Raymond Janis, and, in 1927, the son lost it through delinquent taxes
extraction.Buyer: Frank Read being the present owner; Read had promised to deed 160 acres of the 320 back to Benjamin Janis and keep 160 acres for his trouble and expense of paying these back taxes
extraction.Tax burden forced sale/Mortgage: in 1927, the son lost it through delinquent taxes
extraction.Occupation/Income: Captain of Police, at the Pine Ridge Agency, for the United States Government, which makes up the most of his income; also receives $40.00 pension money each month for having been an Indian Scout
extraction.NOTES: mentally competent; health not so very good, having had two operations, one for appendicitis and one for the kidneys; wife died in 1927; has one child to support; deeded allotment (320 acres) to son Raymond Janis in 1922; son lost it through delinquent taxes in 1927; Read promised to deed 160 acres back to Benjamin Janis but nothing has been said by either party regarding this deal since it passed into the hands of Read; has never received any help from the County, State nor the United States Government outside of pension and police salary; document sworn December 6, 1928
